Vou checar os pontos que controlam exatamente esses dois sintomas: respostas explicativas que viram aviso de grounding e perguntas exatas que não entram no caminho determinístico correto.

Achei o ponto central: o router já está mais forte, mas a ponte determinística ainda não cobre todos os intents que ela mesma marca como determinísticos. E, nas perguntas explicativas, o generative ainda pode ser rejeitado por validações duras demais depois de já produzir uma resposta útil.

Yes. These files are enough to pinpoint both failure modes.

The first problem is a route/handler mismatch. Your router already classifies which symbol owns, what symbol owns, which symbol handles, and similar questions as exact_symbol_locator, so they are supposed to go deterministic.

The second part of that same mismatch is in v10_ai_bridge.py: _is_deterministic_prompt(...) also recognizes those ownership/handler phrases as deterministic triggers, but _answer_deterministic_from_prompt(...) only has concrete handling for file-locator questions and “which calls” questions. There is no dedicated exact-symbol-ownership branch there. So a question like Which symbol owns on_apply_clicked? gets marked deterministic, but the deterministic answer builder returns None, and the request then falls through to the generative path. That is the main reason those exact questions are not getting the answer you expect.

For the answers that get replaced by warning text, the key file is also v10_ai_bridge.py. In the current version, the generative path is still post-validated by _grounding_failure_reason(...), and that method can reject on forbidden_ids, forbidden_paths, and forbidden_symbols, not just on obviously bad hallucinations. Your own bridge metadata also shows _grounding_failure_reason calling _is_generative_prompt, _has_forbidden_ids, and _has_forbidden_paths, which matches the behavior you observed when a decent explanatory answer is generated and then swapped out for a rejection message.

The good news is that the uploaded v10_ai_bridge.py already contains helpful groundwork for code-localized explanations: it extracts snippet blocks, builds a generative focus message, adds snippet anchors to allowed symbols, and adds snippet paths and symbol Location: paths to allowed file paths. That means the bridge is already partially adapted to avoid false rejections for snippet-backed answers. It is closer than before.

v10_main_window.py is also helpful because it confirms the UI/controller routing is not the core bug anymore. ask_local_ai() calls route_query_intent(question) and branches into deterministic, ranked, or generative handlers. It also currently runs with previous-turn merge disabled in debug mode, so stale prior evidence is less likely to be the reason for the blocked answers.

v10_index_loader.py helps on the runtime side. It normalizes runtime source files and explicitly prefers matches inside reasoner_runtime_collector / runtime_collector when resolving runtime paths. That directly supports the runtime-runner snippet resolution problem you were debugging earlier. It does not fix the blocked-answer substitution by itself, but it improves the evidence quality feeding the retriever and bridge.

v10_prompt_builder.py also helps because it now has a dedicated code-localized explanation mode and instructs the model to use real SOURCE SNIPPETS, file paths, anchors, and short grounded excerpts when relevant. So for explanatory questions with code, the prompt side is already pointing in the right direction. The remaining issue is that the bridge can still reject those answers too aggressively afterward.

So the practical conclusion is:

The deterministic failures are mainly caused by v10_ai_bridge.py not yet having an exact-symbol-ownership resolver even though both the router and deterministic prompt detector already classify those questions as deterministic.

The warning-substitution failures are mainly caused by the generative answer being produced and then rejected by post-validation in _grounding_failure_reason(...), especially forbidden_paths and forbidden_symbols.

So yes, these uploaded files do help a lot: they show that your bottleneck is now concentrated in v10_ai_bridge.py, not in the router or the main window. The next fix should be surgical there.
